items.question: How many domains and inboxes do I need for cold email?
items.answer: Work back from your daily volume. Each inbox should send about 30 live emails a day, and we put 4 inboxes on each domain. Our standard setup is 10 domains with 4 inboxes each, 40 inboxes sending up to about 1,200 emails a day. A smaller campaign needs fewer domains.

items.question: Can I send cold email from my main domain?
items.answer: You shouldn't. If a campaign draws spam complaints or bounces, the damage lands on the domain your team uses for clients, invoices and hiring. Send from secondary domains that are close variations of your brand, redirect them to your main website, and keep your main domain for everyday email.

items.question: How long does DNS setup take before I can send?
items.answer: DNS records usually publish within minutes to a few hours and can take up to 48 hours. That is only the start: each new inbox then needs 14 to 21 days of warm-up before its first live cold email. Plan for about three weeks from buying domains to your first campaign.

items.question: Do I need DMARC for cold email?
items.answer: Set it up on every sending domain. Gmail requires DMARC from senders who send more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail accounts, and requires SPF or DKIM from everyone. Start with p=none to monitor, read the reports, and move to p=quarantine once all your legitimate mail passes.
